title: Make Three Strings Equal
summary: Given three strings s1, s2, and s3, you can remove the rightmost character of any string in one operation.
statement: Given three strings s1, s2, and s3, you can remove the rightmost character of any string in one operation. Determine the least number of operations needed to make all strings identical. If it's impossible, return -1.
constraints: Only deletions from the ends of the three strings are allowed.
Make all three resulting strings equal and nonempty using the fewest total deletions.
Return -1 when no nonempty common result is possible.
hints: Any equal result obtainable by end deletion must be a common prefix.
Find the longest prefix shared by all three strings.
If it is empty return -1; otherwise delete every character after it in each string.
Keeping the longest common prefix minimizes deletions, since every shorter feasible prefix removes three additional characters per shortened position.
editorial: Keeping the longest common prefix minimizes deletions, since every shorter feasible prefix removes three additional characters per shortened position.

tests.explanation: Their longest common prefix is ab; deleting c and b costs two.
The first characters already differ, so no nonempty common string is possible.
